verses.zh: 「以色列啊，你当听！你今日要过约旦河，进去赶出比你强大的国民，得着广大坚固、高得顶天的城邑。
verses.en: Listen, Israel: Today you are about to cross the Jordan so you can dispossess the nations there, people greater and stronger than you who live in large cities with extremely high fortifications.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “fortified to the heavens” (so NRSV); NLT “cities with walls that reach to the sky.” This is hyperbole.

verses.zh: 那民是亚衲族的人，又大又高，是你所知道的；也曾听见有人指着他们说：『谁能在亚衲族人面前站立得住呢？』
verses.en: They include the Anakites,[NOTE:1] a numerous[NOTE:2] and tall people whom you know about and of whom it is said, “Who is able to resist the Anakites?”
notes: Anakites. See note on this term in Deut 1:28.
Heb “great and tall.” Many English versions understand this to refer to physical size or strength rather than numbers (cf. “strong,” NIV, NCV, NRSV, NLT).

verses.zh: 你今日当知道，耶和华―你的　神在你前面过去，如同烈火，要灭绝他们，将他们制伏在你面前。这样，你就要照耶和华所说的赶出他们，使他们速速灭亡。
verses.en: Understand today that the Lord your God who goes before you is a devouring fire; he will defeat and subdue them before you. You will dispossess and destroy them quickly just as he[NOTE:1] has told you.
notes: Heb “the Lord.” The pronoun has been used in the translation in keeping with contemporary English style to avoid redundancy.

verses.zh: 「耶和华―你的　神将这些国民从你面前撵出以后，你心里不可说：『耶和华将我领进来得这地是因我的义。』其实，耶和华将他们从你面前赶出去是因他们的恶。
verses.en: Do not think to yourself after the Lord your God has driven them out before you, “Because of my own righteousness the Lord has brought me here to possess this land.” It is because of the wickedness of these nations that the Lord is driving them out ahead of you.

verses.zh: 你进去得他们的地，并不是因你的义，也不是因你心里正直，乃是因这些国民的恶，耶和华―你的　神将他们从你面前赶出去，又因耶和华要坚定他向你列祖亚伯拉罕、以撒、雅各起誓所应许的话。
verses.en: It is not because of your righteousness, or even your inner uprightness,[NOTE:1] that you have come here to possess their land. Instead, because of the wickedness of these nations, the Lord your God is driving them out ahead of you in order to confirm the promise he[NOTE:2] made on oath to your ancestors,[NOTE:3] to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
notes: Heb “uprightness of your heart” (so NASB, NRSV). The Hebrew word צְדָקָה (tsedaqah, “righteousness”), though essentially synonymous here with יֹשֶׁר (yosher, “uprightness”), carries the idea of conformity to an objective standard. The term יֹשֶׁר has more to do with an inner, moral quality (cf. NAB, NIV “integrity”). Neither, however, was grounds for the Lord’s favor. As he states in both vv. 4-5, the main reason he allowed Israel to take this land was the sinfulness of the Canaanites who lived there (cf. Gen 15:16).
Heb “the Lord.” See note on “he” in 9:3.
Heb “fathers.”

verses.zh: 「你当知道，耶和华―你　神将这美地赐你为业，并不是因你的义；你本是硬着颈项的百姓。
verses.en: Understand, therefore, that it is not because of your righteousness that the Lord your God is about to give you this good land as a possession, for you are a stubborn[NOTE:1] people!
notes: The Hebrew word translated stubborn means “stiff-necked.” The image is that of a draft animal that is unsubmissive to the rein or yoke and refuses to bend its neck to draw the load. This is an apt description of OT Israel (Exod 32:9; 33:3, 5; 34:9; Deut 9:13).tn Heb “stiff-necked” (so KJV, NAB, NIV).

verses.zh: 你当记念不忘，你在旷野怎样惹耶和华―你　神发怒。自从你出了埃及地的那日，直到你们来到这地方，你们时常悖逆耶和华。
verses.en: Remember—don’t ever forget[NOTE:1]—how you provoked the Lord your God in the wilderness; from the time you left the land of Egypt until you came to this place you were constantly rebelling against him.[NOTE:2]
notes: By juxtaposing the positive זְכֹר (zekhor, “remember”) with the negative אַל־תִּשְׁכַּח (ʾal tishkakh, “do not forget”), Moses makes a most emphatic plea.
Heb “the Lord” (likewise in the following verse with both “him” and “he”). See note on “he” in 9:3.

verses.zh: 你们在何烈山又惹耶和华发怒；他恼怒你们，要灭绝你们。
verses.en: At Horeb you provoked him and he was angry enough with you to destroy you.

verses.zh: 我上了山，要领受两块石版，就是耶和华与你们立约的版。那时我在山上住了四十昼夜，没有吃饭，也没有喝水。
verses.en: When I went up the mountain to receive the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant that the Lord made with you, I remained there[NOTE:1] 40 days and nights, eating and drinking nothing.
notes: Heb “in the mountain.” The demonstrative pronoun has been used in the translation for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 耶和华把那两块石版交给我，是　神用指头写的。版上所写的是照耶和华在大会的日子、在山上、从火中对你们所说的一切话。
verses.en: The Lord gave me the two stone tablets, written by the very finger[NOTE:1] of God, and on them was everything[NOTE:2] he[NOTE:3] said to you at the mountain from the midst of the fire at the time of that assembly.
notes: The very finger of God. This is a double figure of speech (1) in which God is ascribed human features (anthropomorphism) and (2) in which a part stands for the whole (synecdoche). That is, God, as Spirit, has no literal finger nor, if he had, would he write with his finger. Rather, the sense is that God himself—not Moses in any way—was responsible for the composition of the Ten Commandments (cf. Exod 31:18; 32:16; 34:1).
Heb “according to all the words.”
Heb “the Lord” (likewise at the beginning of vv. 12, 13). See note on “he” in 9:3.

verses.zh: 过了四十昼夜，耶和华把那两块石版，就是约版，交给我。
verses.en: Now at the end of the 40 days and nights the Lord presented me with the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant.

verses.zh: 对我说：『你起来，赶快下去！因为你从埃及领出来的百姓已经败坏了自己；他们快快地偏离了我所吩咐的道，为自己铸成了偶像。』
verses.en: And he said to me, “Get up, go down at once from here because your people whom you brought out of Egypt have sinned! They have quickly turned from the way I commanded them and have made for themselves a cast metal image.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “a casting.” The MT reads מַסֵּכָה (massekhah, “a cast thing”) but some mss and Smr add עֵגֶל (ʿegel, “calf”), “a molten calf” or the like (Exod 32:8). Perhaps Moses here omits reference to the calf out of contempt for it.

verses.zh: 「耶和华又对我说：『我看这百姓是硬着颈项的百姓。
verses.en: Moreover, he said to me, “I have taken note of these people; they are a stubborn[NOTE:1] lot!
notes: Heb “stiff-necked.” See note on the word “stubborn” in 9:6.

verses.zh: 你且由着我，我要灭绝他们，将他们的名从天下涂抹，使你的后裔比他们成为更大更强的国。』
verses.en: Stand aside[NOTE:1] and I will destroy them, obliterating their very name from memory,[NOTE:2] and I will make you into a stronger and more numerous nation than they are.”
notes: Heb “leave me alone.”
Heb “from under heaven.”

verses.zh: 于是我转身下山，山被火烧着，两块约版在我两手之中。
verses.en: So I turned and went down the mountain while it[NOTE:1] was blazing with fire; the two tablets of the covenant were in my hands.
notes: Heb “the mountain.” The translation uses a pronoun for stylistic reasons to avoid redundancy.

verses.zh: 我一看见你们得罪了耶和华―你们的　神，铸成了牛犊，快快地偏离了耶和华所吩咐你们的道，
verses.en: When I looked, you had indeed sinned against the Lord your God and had cast for yourselves a metal calf;[NOTE:1] you had quickly turned aside from the way he[NOTE:2] had commanded you!
notes: On the phrase “metal calf,” see note on the term “metal image” in v. 12.
Heb “the Lord.” See note on “he” in 9:3.

verses.zh: 我就把那两块版从我手中扔下去，在你们眼前摔碎了。
verses.en: I grabbed the two tablets, threw them down,[NOTE:1] and shattered them before your very eyes.
notes: The Hebrew text includes “from upon my two hands,” but as this seems somewhat obvious and redundant, it has been left untranslated for stylistic reasons.

verses.zh: 因你们所犯的一切罪，行了耶和华眼中看为恶的事，惹他发怒，我就像从前俯伏在耶和华面前四十昼夜，没有吃饭，也没有喝水。
verses.en: Then I again fell down before the Lord for 40 days and nights; I ate and drank nothing because of all the sin you had committed, doing such evil before the Lord as to enrage him.

verses.zh: 我因耶和华向你们大发烈怒，要灭绝你们，就甚害怕；但那次耶和华又应允了我。
verses.en: For I was terrified at the Lord’s intense anger[NOTE:1] that threatened to destroy you. But he[NOTE:2] listened to me this time as well.
notes: Heb “the anger and the wrath.” Although many English versions translate as two terms, this construction is a hendiadys which serves to intensify the emotion (cf. NAB, TEV “fierce anger”).
Heb “the Lord.” See note on “he” in 9:3.

verses.zh: 耶和华也向亚伦甚是发怒，要灭绝他；那时我又为亚伦祈祷。
verses.en: The Lord was also angry enough at Aaron to kill him, but at that time I prayed for him[NOTE:1] too.
notes: Heb “Aaron.” The pronoun is used in the translation to avoid redundancy.

verses.zh: 我把那叫你们犯罪所铸的牛犊用火焚烧，又捣碎磨得很细，以致细如灰尘，我就把这灰尘撒在从山上流下来的溪水中。
verses.en: As for your sinful thing[NOTE:1] that you had made, the calf, I took it, melted it down,[NOTE:2] ground it up until it was as fine as dust, and tossed the dust into the stream that flows down the mountain.
notes: Heb “your sin.” This is a metonymy in which the effect (sin) stands for the cause (the metal calf).
Heb “burned it with fire.”

verses.zh: 「你们在他备拉、玛撒、基博罗・哈他瓦又惹耶和华发怒。
verses.en: Moreover, you continued to provoke the Lord at Taberah,[NOTE:1] Massah,[NOTE:2] and Kibroth Hattaavah.[NOTE:3]
notes: Taberah. By popular etymology this derives from the Hebrew verb בָעַר (baʿar, “to burn”), thus, here, “burning.” The reference is to the Lord’s fiery wrath against Israel because of their constant complaints against him (Num 11:1-3).
Massah. See note on this term in Deut 6:16.

Kibroth Hattaavah. This place name means in Hebrew “burial places of appetite,” that is, graves that resulted from overindulgence. The reference is to the Israelites stuffing themselves with the quail God had provided and doing so with thanklessness (Num 11:31-35).

verses.zh: 耶和华打发你们离开加低斯・巴尼亚，说：『你们上去得我所赐给你们的地。』那时你们违背了耶和华―你们　神的命令，不信服他，不听从他的话。
verses.en: And when he[NOTE:1] sent you from Kadesh Barnea and told you, “Go up and possess the land I have given you,” you rebelled against the Lord your God[NOTE:2] and would neither believe nor obey him.
notes: Heb “the Lord.” See note on “he” in 9:3.
Heb “the mouth of the Lord your God,” that is, against the commandment that he had spoken.

verses.zh: 自从我认识你们以来，你们常常悖逆耶和华。
verses.en: You have been rebelling against him[NOTE:1] from the very first day I knew you!
notes: Heb “the Lord.” See note on “he” in 9:3.

verses.zh: 「我因耶和华说要灭绝你们，就在耶和华面前照旧俯伏四十昼夜。
verses.en: I lay flat on the ground before the Lord for 40 days and nights,[NOTE:1] for he[NOTE:2] had said he would destroy you.
notes: The Hebrew text includes “when I prostrated myself.” Since this is redundant, it has been left untranslated.
Heb “the Lord.” See note on “he” in 9:3.

verses.zh: 我祈祷耶和华说：『主耶和华啊，求你不要灭绝你的百姓。他们是你的产业，是你用大力救赎的，用大能从埃及领出来的。
verses.en: I prayed to him:[NOTE:1] O, Sovereign Lord,[NOTE:2] do not destroy your people, your valued property[NOTE:3] that you have powerfully redeemed,[NOTE:4] whom you brought out of Egypt by your strength.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “the Lord.” See note on “he” in 9:3.
Heb “Lord Yahweh” (אֲדֹנָי יְהוִה, ʾadonay yehvih). The phrase is customarily rendered by Jewish tradition as “Lord God” (אֲדֹנָי אֱלֹהִים, ʾadonay ʾelohim).
Heb “your inheritance”; NLT “your special (very own NRSV) possession.” Israel is compared to landed property that one would inherit from his ancestors and pass on to his descendants.
Heb “you have redeemed in your greatness.”
Heb “by your strong hand.”

verses.zh: 求你记念你的仆人亚伯拉罕、以撒、雅各，不要想念这百姓的顽梗、邪恶、罪过，
verses.en: Remember your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob; ignore the stubbornness, wickedness, and sin of these people.

verses.zh: 免得你领我们出来的那地之人说，耶和华因为不能将这百姓领进他所应许之地，又因恨他们，所以领他们出去，要在旷野杀他们。
verses.en: Otherwise the people of the land[NOTE:1] from which you brought us will say, “The Lord was unable to bring them to the land he promised them, and because of his hatred for them he has brought them out to kill them in the wilderness.”
notes: The MT reads only “the land.” Smr supplies עַם (ʿam, “people”) and LXX and its dependents supply “the inhabitants of the land.” The truncated form found in the MT is adequate to communicate the intended meaning; the words “the people of” are supplied in the translation for clarity.

verses.zh: 其实他们是你的百姓，你的产业，是你用大能和伸出来的膀臂领出来的。』」
verses.en: They are your people, your valued property,[NOTE:1] whom you brought out with great strength and power.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “your inheritance.” See note at v. 26.
Heb “an outstretched arm.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see "Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are responsible for your
own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation.
You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: DEUTERONOMY 9:1-6

1"Hear, O Israel! You are crossing over the Jordan today to go in to dispossess nations greater and mightier than you,
great cities fortified to heaven, 2a people great and tall, the sons of the Anakim, whom you know and of whom you have heard
it said,' Who can stand before the sons of Anak?' 3Know therefore today that it is the Lord your
God who is crossing over before you as a consuming fire. He will destroy them and He will subdue them before you, so that you may drive them
out and destroy them quickly, just as the Lord has spoken to you. 4Do not say in your heart when the
Lord your God has driven them out before you, 'Because of my righteousness the Lord
has brought me in to possess this land,' but it is because of the wickedness of these nations that the Lord
is dispossessing them before you. 5It is not for your righteousness or for the uprightness of your heart that you are going to possess their
land, but it is because of the wickedness of these nations that the Lord your God is driving them out before
you, in order to confirm the oath which the Lord swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. 6Know,
then, it is not because of your righteousness that the Lord your God is giving you this good land to possess,
for you are a stubborn people."

9:1 "Hear" This is the Hebrew term shema (BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE,
cf. Deut. 4:1; 5:1; 6:3,4; 9:1; 20:3; 27:9), which means "to hear so as to do." See note at Deut. 4:1.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema

▣ "O Israel" See SPECIAL TOPIC: ISRAEL (the name).

▣ "nations greater and mightier than you" This is a repeated theme (see note at Deut. 1:28). The theological
point (i.e. YHWH's sovereign choice and His promise to the Patriarchs) is in Deut. 7:6-9. He is trustworthy and true. His faithful,
loving character is magnified in Israel's stubbornness and stiffneckedness (cf. Deut. 9:6,7,13,24,27; 10:16; 31:27).

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS

9:2 "the Anakim. . .sons of Anak" Etymologically this term means "long neck" and, therefore, refers to the giants.

- In Deut. 2:10-11 they are linked to the Rephaim

- in Num. 13:33 they are linked to the Nephilim

SPECIAL TOPIC: TERMS USED FOR TALL/POWERFUL WARRIORS OR PEOPLE GROUPS (Giants)

SPECIAL TOPIC: "sons of God" in Genesis 6

▣ "know" See full note at Deut. 4:35.

9:3 "Know" This VERB (BDB 393, KB 390, Qal PERFECT with waw)
is used often and in several senses.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

▣ "a consuming fire" This is BDB 77 plus BDB 37, Qal ACTIVE PARTICIPAL.
This imagery is describing the judgment of God on the people of the land because of their wickedness (cf. v.4-5;
Gen 15:16). See note at Deut. 4:24. For a good brief discussion of the imagery used to describe God see
The Dictionary of Biblical Imagery, pp.332-336.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE

▣ "He will destroy them and He will subdue them before you" These two VERBS of
conquest are parallel and denote YHWH's actions on Israel's behalf:

- "destroy" ‒ BDB 1029, KB 1552, Hiphil IMPERFECT

- "subdue" ‒ BDB 488, KB 484, Hiphil IMPERFECT

Also note that Israel must act in faith and attack:

- "you may drive them out" ‒ BDB 439, KB 441, Hiphil PERFECT with waw

- "destroy them quickly" ‒ BDB 1, KB 2, Hiphil PERFECT with waw
plus the ADVERB (BDB 555 II)

Notice the theological and covenantal balance between the promised action of the sovereign
YHWH and the mandated faithful response of the Israeli army and leaders. Both are crucial!

It is also to be noted that YHWH accomplished His task, but Israel did not complete the task of
totally removing the indigenous inhabitants (cf. Judges 1-2). Israel should have acted quickly (cf. Deut. 7:22), but
she did not!

9:4-6 "Do not say in your heart when the Lord your God has driven them out before
you, 'Because of my righteousness'" This is similar to Deut. 8:11-20. God is showing the people again that He is acting,
not because they are good, but because of

- the wickedness of the people in the land (cf. Gen. 15:12-21; Lev. 18:24-25; 20:13-14)

- His promise to their Patriarchs beginning in Gen. 12:1-3

He wants them to remember that He is in full control.

The initial VERB "say" (BDB 55, KB 65) is a Qal IMPERFECT,
used in a JUSSIVE sense. The fallen heart of humanity is still ever present and spiritually dangerous.

The second VERB "has driven" (BDB 213, KB 239, Qal INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT) shows
YHWH's active involvement in the Conquest (cf. Deut. 6:19; JosH. 23:5).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S GRACE ACTS TO ISRAEL

9:5 "It is not for your righteousness or for the uprightness of your heart" These two NOUNS are
parallel in this context:

- "righteousness" ‒ BDB 842, cf. Deut. 6:25; 9:4,5,6; 24:13; 33:21, see
SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

- "uprightness" ‒ BDB 449, means integrity or moral lifestyle, cf. 1 Chr. 29:17; Ps. 119:7

Israel is not being given the land Canaan because of her godliness, but because of

- the Canaanite's ungodliness (cf. Deut. 9:4; Gen. 15:12-21; Lev. 18:24-28, see note at Deut. 3:6)

- YHWH's greater purpose for Israel

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

▣ "to confirm the oath the Lord swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac
and Jacob" Notice the VERBS:

- "to confirm the oath" ‒ BDB 877, KB 1086, Hiphil INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT

- "the Lord swore" ‒ BDB 989, KB 1396, Niphal PERFECT

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT PROMISES TO THE PATRIARCHS

▣ "righteousness" See SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

9:6, 13 "you are a stubborn people" This was originally an agricultural phrase referring to unruly oxen. Literally
this means "hard of neck" or "stiff-necked" (BDB 904 CONSTRUCT BDB 791, cf. Deut. 9:6,7,13,24,27; 10:16;
31:27; Exod. 32:9; 33:3,5; 34:9).

SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS (OT)

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: DEUTERONOMY 9:7-21

7 "Remember, do not forget how you provoked the Lord
your God to wrath in the wilderness; from the day that you left the land of Egypt until you arrived at this place, you have been rebellious against the
Lord. 8Even at Horeb you provoked the Lord to wrath, and the
Lord was so angry with you that He would have destroyed you. 9When I went up to the mountain to receive
the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant which the Lord had made with you, then I remained on the mountain forty
days and nights; I neither ate bread nor drank water. 10And the Lord gave me the two tablets of stone written
by the finger of God; and on them were all the words which the Lord had spoken with you at the mountain from the
midst of the fire on the day of the assembly. 11And it came about at the end of forty days and nights that the Lord
gave me the two tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant. 12Then the Lord said to me, 'Arise, go down from
here quickly, for your people whom you brought out of Egypt have acted corruptly. They have quickly turned aside from the way which I commanded them; they
have made a molten image for themselves.' 13The Lord spoke further to me, saying, 'I have seen this people, and
indeed, it is a stubborn people. 14Let Me alone, that I may destroy them and blot out their name from under heaven; and I will make of you a nation
mightier and greater than they.' 15So I turned and came down from the mountain while the mountain was burning with fire, and the two tablets of the
covenant were in my two hands. 16And I saw that you had indeed sinned against the Lord your God. You had made for
yourselves a molten calf; you had turned aside quickly from the way which the Lord had commanded you. 17And I took
hold of the two tablets and threw them from my hands, and smashed them before your eyes. 18And I fell down before the Lord,
as at the first, forty days and nights; I neither ate bread nor drank water, because of all your sin which you had committed in doing what was evil in the sight of the
Lord to provoke Him to anger. 19For I was afraid of the anger and hot displeasure with which the Lord
was wrathful against you in order to destroy you, but the Lord listened to me that time also. 20And the Lord
was angry enough with Aaron to destroy him; so I also prayed for Aaron at the same time. 21And I took your sinful thing, the calf which you had made,
and burned it with fire and crushed it, grinding it very small until it was as fine as dust; and I threw its dust into the brook that came down from the mountain."

9:7 "Remember, do not forget" These two initial VERBS (BDB 269, KB 269, Qal IMPERATIVES,
cf. Deut. 5:15; 7:18 [twice]; 8:2; 9:7,27; 15:15; 16:3,12; 24:9,18,22; 25:17; 32:7 and BDB 1013, KB 1489, Qal IMPERFECT,
functioning as a JUSSIVE, cf. Deut. 4:9,23; 6:12; 8:11,14,19 [twice]; 9:7) are to help Israel remember (see note at Deut. 7:18)
and not repeat her lack of faith in YHWH, His promises and His power as they did on several occasions during the exodus and
wilderness wandering period.

Moses mentions their act of idolatry and rebellion at the foot of Mt. Horeb in Deut. 9:8, where Aaron
fashioned a golden calf at the insistence of the people (cf. Exodus 32)!

9:7-8 "how you provoked the Lord" See Exodus 16; 32; and Numbers 13-14; 16:21,25
as some examples.

9:7-22 These verses refer to the actions of Israel while Moses was on Mt. Horeb/Sinai receiving the Law (cf. Exodus 32).

▣ "Horeb" See SPECIAL TOPIC: LOCATION OF MT. SINAI and
SPECIAL TOPIC: HOREB

9:9 "the tablets of stone, the tablets of the covenant which the Lord had made with you"
Obviously the phrase "tablets of stone, and the tablets of the covenant" are parallel. These were YHWH's words,
not Moses'. This is revelation, not human opinion or discovery.

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TEN COMMANDMENTS

9:9,11,18 "forty days" This number is often symbolic of a long, indefinite period of time, longer than a lunar cycle
(i.e. 28 days) but less than a seasonal change. The time from leaving Mt. Horeb/Sinai to entering Canaan was thirty eight years.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #7

9:9, 18 "I neither ate bread nor drank water" This refers to two separate 40 day fasts meaning either

- a miraculous preservation (cf. Exod. 24:18; 34:28)

- a hyperbolic idiom for a limited fast (no food, but water)

This same period of fasting is used of Jesus in Matt. 4; Luke 4. He is the "new" Moses!

9:10 "the two tablets of stone" Because of Hittite Suzerain Treaties as a possible historical background, this
may refer to two complete copies of the Law. See introduction to the book, VII.

SPECIAL TOPIC: HITTITE (SUZERAIN) TREATIES

▣ "written by the finger of God" This is imagery for the divine origin of the Ten Words and their
explanations (cf. Exod. 31:18; 32:15-16; Deut. 4:13).

SPECIAL TOPIC: GOD DESCRIBED AS HUMAN (Anthropomorphic Language)

▣ "the Lord had spoken with you at the mountain from the midst of the fire" This
is a recurrent theme (cf. Deut. 4:12,15,33,36; 5:5,22,24,26; 9:10; 10:4). The phrase emphasizes God's acts and the content of
the personal covenant revelation at Mt. Horeb/Sinai (i.e. Exod. 19-20).

9:12-14 Moses remembers his dialogue with YHWH in Exodus 32

- "arise," Deut. 9:12 ‒ BDB 877, KB 1086, Qal IMPERATIVE

- "go down," Deut. 9:12 ‒ BDB 432, KB 434, Qal IMPERATIVE

- "let Me alone," Deut. 9:14 ‒ BDB 951, KB 1276, Hiphil IMPERATIVE

a COHORTATIVE sense

a COHORTATIVE sense

PERFECT) is used many times of YHWH, but only here of Moses.

▣ "turned aside" This VERB (BDB 693, KB747, Qal PERFECT) is
theologically parallel to שׁוב (BDB 996, KB 1427). This Hebrew root can denote idolatry or repentance.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CONSEQUENCES OF IDOLATRY

SPECIAL TOPIC: REPENTANCE (OT)

▣ "molten image" This (BDB 651) does not refer to idolatry, but a physical representation of YHWH. This was a violation of

9:14 Is this an example of the wrath of God or is it a test of Moses' leadership (cf. Deut. 9:25ff, Exod. 32:30-35)?

▣ "blot out their name from under heaven" This is Hebrew imagery (cf. Deut. 25:5; Ps. 41:5) for the
complete extermination of the covenant people, except Moses.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TWO BOOKS OF GOD

22 "Again at Taberah and at Massah and at Kibroth-hattaavah you provoked
the Lord to wrath. 23And when the Lord sent you from Kadesh-barnea,
saying, 'Go up and possess the land which I have given you,' then you rebelled against the command of the Lord your

9:22 "Taberah" This was one of the campsites of Israel (mentioned in Numbers 33). The place name
comes from a word play on the VERB "to burn" (BDB 129). This was
the geographical location where YHWH answered their constant complaining with a judgment of fire (cf. Num. 11:1-3,34-35).
It was about a three day journey north of Mt. Horeb/Sinai, but the exact location is uncertain.

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE EXODUS, III.

▣ "Massah" This was another location of conflict between YHWH and Israel during the exodus
(cf. Exod. 17:7). It is usually linked to Meribah (cf. Deut. 33:8), but not always (cf. Deut. 6:16; 9:2).

- Massah means "testing" (BDB 650 III, cf. Deut. 6:16; 9:22; 33:8; Exod. 17:7; Ps. 95:8)

- Meribah means "strife" (BDB 937 II, cf. Exod. 17:7)

▣ "Kibroth-Hattaavah" The name means "graves of lust" (BDB 869, cf. Num. 11:31-35). Numbers 11
mentions movement recorded between Taberah and Kibroth-Hattaavah, but here in Deuteronomy the two sites are separate.

9:23 "Go up and possess this land" These are both Qal IMPERATIVES and reflect
YHWH's direct speech through Moses to Israel:

- "go up" ‒ BDB 748, KB 828

- "possess" ‒ BDB 439, KB 441 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: POSSESS THE LAND)

Notice again YHWH's command for Israel to act on her belief in His sovereignty and promises. But
instead of faith Israel demonstrated unbelief:

- "you rebelled against the command" ‒ BDB 598, KB 632 , Hiphil IMPERFECT with waw,
cf. Num. 20:24; 27:14; Deut. 1:26,43; 9:23; Ps. 107:11

- "you neither believed Him" ‒ BDB 52, KB 63, Hiphil PERFECT

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVE, TRUST, FAITH AND FAITHFULNESS IN THE OT

- "nor listened to His voice" ‒ BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal PERFECT (these Qal
PERFECTS reflect a settled condition). This is exactly opposite of covenant obedience and responsibility.

SPECIAL TOPIC: LISTEN/HEAR (shema)

- Hithpael PERFECT, Deut. 9:25

SPECIAL TOPIC: INTERCESSORY PRAYER

▣ "forty days and nights" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SYMBOLIC NUMBERS IN SCRIPTURE, #7

9:26-29 Verses 26-29 show three reasons Moses gave to YHWH in answer to His question, "Why should I spare Israel?":

- His promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob (cf. Exod. 32:13)

- Canaan will misunderstand YHWH's character

- Canaan will not understand YHWH's judgment on Israel

The paragraph contains three prayer request VERBS:

- "do not destroy," Deut. 9:26 ‒ BDB 1007, KB 1469, Hiphil JUSSIVE

- "remember," Deut. 9:27 ‒ BDB 269, KB 269, Qal IMPERATIVE

- "do not look" (i.e. "turn"), Deut. 9:27 ‒ BDB 815, KB 937, Qal JUSSIVE

Moses appeals to YHWH's character and eternal redemptive plan for all people as the basis for not
destroying His disobedient covenant people. More is at stake than just one people group!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

9:26 Notice how Moses' prayer reminds YHWH of His covenant relationship:

- "Lord God" (literally, "adon YHWH," cf. Deut. 3:24 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: Lord [adon and kurios])

- "Thy people" ‒ covenant title, cf. Deut. 9:29

- "Thine inheritance" ‒ covenant gift, cf. Deut. 9:29

- "Thou has redeemed ‒ BDB 804, KB 911, Qal PERFECT (see SPECIAL TOPIC: RANSOM/REDEEM).
YHWH delivered them from slavery to a national entity (cf. Deut. 7:8; 9:26; 13:5)

- "Thou hast brought out of Egypt" ‒ BDB 422, KB 425, Hiphil PERFECT; this fulfilled YHWH's covenant promise
to Abraham (cf. Deut. 9:29; Gen. 15:16-21)

YHWH acts because of who He is! He follows the redemptive plan He has for all peoples! The great hope of all mankind is the
unchanging, gracious, merciful, loving character of YHWH (e.g. Exod. 34:6; Mal. 3:6). See notes at Deut. 4:31 and 10:17.

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

▣ "with a mighty hand" This phrase and "outstretched arm" of Deut. 9:29 have both been found in Egyptian
texts referring to the Egyptian king. This is a recurrent idiom (cf. Exod. 32:11; Deut. 4:34; 5:15; 6:21; 7:8,19; 9:26; 11:2; 26:8;
34:12; 2 Chr. 6:32; Ps. 136:12; Dan. 9:15). Moses chose phrases that Israel had heard before in relationship to Pharaoh. YHWH
was their true king!

9:27 Notice the character of Israel:

- "the stubbornness of this people" ‒ BDB 904, cf. Deut. 9:6,7,13,24,27 (see SPECIAL TOPIC: STUBBORNNESS)

- "their wickedness" ‒ BDB 957, cf. Jer. 14:20; Ezek. 3:19; 33:12

- "their sin" ‒ BDB 308, cf. Exod. 32:30; Deut. 9:18; Ps. 32:5; 51:5; Prov. 5:22; 13:6; 14:34; 21:4; 24:9 (Deuteronomy
shares the vocabulary of the sages)

purpose of redemption, spare Israel. Another phrase used in the same sense is, "for God's namesake" (cf. Isa. 48:9-11;
Ezek. 20:9,14,22,44; 36:21-23; Dan. 9:17-19).

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- Why did God choose Israel?

- Is Deut. 9:14 a true reflection of God's nature? If not, what is it?

- List and discuss the three reasons Moses gives as to why YHWH should not destroy Israel.
